title: low danube river levels force romania shut down both its nuclear power reactors 2026 07 29
text:
BUCHAREST, July 29 (Reuters) - Romania will shut down its ‌second nuclear reactor on the Danube river, the energy ministry said on Wednesday, three days after decades-low river levels forced it to shut down the first.
State-owned nuclear power producer ​Nuclearelectrica (ROSNN.BX)
, opens new tab
 has two 706-megawatt reactors at Cernavoda on the Danube, accounting ​for roughly a fifth of Romania's power production. The two ⁠reactors have never before been disconnected from the grid at the same ​time because of low water levels.
The second reactor's shutdown scheduled for early ​Thursday will increase Romania's reliance on imports and pressure power prices that have already been increased by heatwave conditions in much of Europe that have driven demand for air conditioning.
In ​Romania, the energy ministry said on Monday peak power consumption this week ​was estimated at 7.3 GW, while domestic production was at up to 4.3 GW, prior ‌to ⁠the second reactor's shutdown. Romania's production is at 7 GW on average.
Low river levels have also forced neighbouring Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant to shut down one of its four reactors.
The level at the Romanian entry point of ​the Danube river fell ​to 1,650 cubic ⁠metres of water per second on Tuesday, the state water-management agency said, against a July average range of ​4,750 cubic metres per second.
The agency said levels of the Danube, ​Europe's second-longest ⁠river, are estimated to fall to 1,500 cubic metres of water per second on August 4, compared with an all-time low of 1,400 recorded in ⁠1985.
The average ​peak temperature across Western Europe on Wednesday ​was forecast to be 31 degrees Celsius (87.8 degrees Fahrenheit), 7.4 degrees above the normal high for ​July 29, the Reuters Climate Monitor shows.
